WP-C1-1-06.note: P02-B04, P02-B05 and P02-B07 are fully applied; P02-B03 is partial. P02-B04: approved() and the denied path in done build the proof locally, commit backend.client_permission, then assign permission. done is chained with .finally(ready), so admission always settles; the remaining done.catch only suppresses an unhandled rejection. P02-B05: prepareProviderClientEffect checks remainingChildBudget(owner).toolCalls before reserveToolCalls, like the read path. P02-B07: the outer 'Provider stream' abortable uses PROVIDER_CLEANUP_GRACE_MS. P02-B03 (approved decision a): the dispatch gate no longer uses abortable. It rejects with effectSignal.reason through a once listener that is removed when the gate opens, then checkAbort and the original-request check run as before. Resolved scenario: the agent ends its turn without the wire write, so native-effects close() cancels the effect. The effect now settles as tool 'failed' (CANCELLED), completion errorCode BACKEND_CLIENT_EFFECT_FAILED, cleanupConfirmed true, in about 0.3 s instead of 1 s. Before, the run ended CLEANUP_UNCERTAIN and the effect stayed uncertain. Remaining scenario: a user/Run cancel while the approved effect waits at the gate. The gate stall is gone (0.34 s vs 1.36 s at BASE), and the tool is interrupted with the cancel reason instead of the gate cleanup message. But settleClientRead still fails with BACKEND_EFFECT_PART_INVALID: an interrupted tool's Part stays 'open' until TurnExecutor.finishParts runs at Turn end, after backend close(). So the effect is still marked uncertain and the Run still fails CLEANUP_UNCERTAIN, as at BASE. Fixing that means closing the interrupted client-effect Part early, which changes TurnExecutor Part lifecycle (turn-executor.ts). That is outside this package's files and risk budget, so it was left for a follow-up and no test pins the current outcome.

WP-C2-1-11.note: Already integrated in f240ac0. Fixes P21-B03 on Linux and FreeBSD. When the shell exits on its own, the supervisor lists the processes left in the PTY session by session id, cleans each group the way stop() does, and confirms cleanup only when a second listing finds none. If a live process holds the shell pid, the pid was reused and nothing is signalled. Partial because macOS ps reports no session id and no ancestry snapshot exists before a normal exit. macOS keeps the original-group probe, and engine-process-terminals.md documents this limit.

WP-X-3-22.note: P15-S02 split done: new schedules/journal.ts has class ScheduleJournal(db, clock = Date.now). It holds the record, proof and receipt types, the helpers (fail, json, signed, fields, payload, digest, id, integer), the administrative headroom constants, row/read/head/receipt/duplicate/sizes/administrativeReserve/insert/commit/revise, target/scheduleFor, getSchedule/getLease/getOccurrence/inspectSchedules/inspectOccurrences, inputRecord/inputProof/observation/recoveryRecord and semantic/validate/pauseImported. It also exports validateScheduleDatabase and markImportedSchedulesDisabled, which now build new ScheduleJournal(db) instead of the historical() table of denied ports. store.ts keeps ScheduleTriggerProof, ScheduleStoragePorts, the inputs and results, Cap, data and sync. In store.ts, ScheduleStorage extends ScheduleJournal with the port-using operations, occurrenceBudget/candidateRecord, recoverInterrupted and lookupScheduleInput. Its constructor passes super(db, () => ports.now?.() ?? Date.now()), so tests that change ports.now still work. Code moved verbatim; only private became protected and some declarations became exports, which a line-multiset diff confirmed. WP-C3-1-17's triggerKey dedupe, claim-time clock checks and recovery headroom are untouched, and the writer and auditor rules both stay. Not done: moving the journal primitives onto storage/revision-journal.ts. Schedule, lease and occurrence bodies have no kind or entityId, which the journal's decode, write, head, receiptOf and assertHeads all use. Receipt rows store entity_id as kind:entity while the receipt body's entityId is the bare entity. Trigger receipts carry expectedScheduleRevision and due-occurrence receipts no expectedRevision, which receiptOf requires. Per-read request_scope and receipt createdAt checks would be lost. Fitting all of this would need several journal hooks for one adopter, the same reason U110 kept workflows off the journal.
